newsitem.title: IRAN: Quake victims in tents in snow-swept Iran region.
newsitem.headline: Quake victims in tents in snow-swept Iran region.

text.p: Relief workers have resettled tens of thousands of people whose homes were destroyed by an earthquake last week in the snow-swept mountains of northwest Iran, Tehran Radio said on Thursday.

The operation to settle more than 36,000 people made homeless by Friday's quake has ended and the victims have been resettled in tents and other temporary shelters in the agricultural region, the radio said.

It said 11,000 tents, 30,000 blankets, 200 tonnes of bread, 15,000 stoves, 95 tonnes of dates and 157,000 tins of food had been distributed to survivors of the quake, which measured 5.5 on the Richter scale.
Nearly 1,000 people were killed and 2,600 injured in the quake, which disrupted the lives of 60,000 people. It was followed by 500 aftershocks and another quake measuring 5.2 on Sunday night.
At least 200 school children were among those killed in the quake which destroyed 90 schools, the official news agency IRNA said.
Up to 20 villages were completely destroyed and 80 others damaged. Heavy damage was also caused to roads, power lines, water supplies, schools and rural clinics.

IRNA said aid from Turkey, Oman, Tunisia, Jordan, Japan, Germany, Azerbaijan and Saudi Arabia had either been sent or was on its way. Iran on Tuesday issued an international appeal for help through the United Nations.
The agency made no mention of the $25,000 the United States said it was donating.
The United Nations had said Norway and Denmark also pledged aid and it expected more donations. Iran earlier said Switzerland, Britain, Japan and some international organisations had offered aid.
Iran said it needed food, clothing, tents, heaters, medicine, the reconstruction of clinics, water and power networks, agricultural equipment, seeds and ambulances.
